Healthcare costs are crushing hardworking Granite Staters. 

You are not alone, and our office and healthcare navigators like Mariana are here to help and support you: https://t.co/3ud3p9fLQZ https://t.co/IO6JQPOzqp
"Goodlander relentless in fight for lower health insurance." https://t.co/kJfeLkgdeT

In a matter of hours, this senseless government shutdown will be the longest in American history.
 
You deserve better. @SpeakerJohnson: reopen the House of Representatives so we can end this shutdown, prevent a full-blown healthcare crisis, and deliver for the American people. https://t.co/xKAneyZgsj

The extraordinary community healthcare providers and first responders I met today at @Spearememorial — our critical access hospital in Plymouth — are feeling the pain of the biggest cuts to healthcare in American history. They are being asked to do more with less and less every day, but they never lose sight of their mission: delivering life-changing and life-saving care to our fellow citizens across the beating heart of the 603.  

I will never stop fighting for them with every tool I’ve got in Congress.

Every Granite Stater deserves the dignity of quality and affordable care close to home.

Mid-State Health Center is the backbone of healthcare for thousands of families across the beating heart of the 603. I loved spending time with them in Thornton earlier this week and I’m grateful to be working alongside them to protect the healthcare you and your family rely on.
I’m focused on reopening our government and protecting the healthcare of millions of people across our country and our state. https://t.co/E2XpjTjxUV

Every American should get the healthcare they need when they need it and where they need it. But most Americans (more than 70% here in New Hampshire) are delaying or just straight up not getting the healthcare they need. 

Why? Healthcare costs too much — too much money and too much time.💰⏰

We must cut healthcare costs (💰and ⏰), and getting the job done will take serious people of good faith in *both* the Senate and the People’s House.

So Majority Leader Thune and Leader Schumer: Let’s get to work. 

⬇️ Read our letter here ⬇️

I spoke with Ann, a single mom of two boys from Pembroke, who will see her family’s healthcare costs skyrocket to nearly $40,000 next year if Congress doesn’t take action.

Totally unaffordable and unacceptable.

That’s why I’m using every tool I’ve got to protect your healthcare and lower your costs.

H.R. 1, President Trump’s so-called “Big, Beautiful Bill,” is jacking up healthcare costs and driving our best healthcare providers out of business. 

This is a matter of life and death, and I won’t quit doing everything in my power to lower crushing costs and protect the care that is a lifeline for millions of hardworking Americans.

Every American should get the healthcare they need when they need it and where they need it. Today most people in New Hampshire are not. Hardworking Americans, including Alice from Peterborough, are getting crushed by sky-high costs, the GOP’s historic healthcare cuts, and corporate greed. 

I’m never going to quit in my mission to protect the care Granite Staters rely on and lower your costs across the board.
Right now, we are living through a healthcare cost crisis. Tackling it should bring us all together as Americans. That’s what I’m working to do in Congress. https://t.co/HbI8ZHAT2m
We need to return the power in our healthcare system back to people and crack down on corporate abuses of power that are jacking up costs and undermining quality. https://t.co/hgyCyPq22A

🚨Today, we launched a bipartisan coalition and commonsense plan to address our healthcare cost crisis. 

Lowering the sky-high cost of healthcare is a matter of life or death for people across New Hampshire. Tens of thousands of Granite Staters are just days away from losing their healthcare. Congress must act, and the commonsense plan and bipartisan coalition we launched are mission-critical to protecting your healthcare and lowering your costs.  

Let’s get this done.

Lowering the sky-high cost of healthcare is a matter of life or death for families across New Hampshire.

That’s why today I’m introducing bipartisan legislation that will save the healthcare tens of thousands of Granite Staters risk losing at the end of this month. Our bill will also kickstart commonsense reforms to cut costs and empower people by cracking down on the big corporations that are jacking up your healthcare costs. 

Let’s get this done.

🚨Granite Staters: Today is the final day to enroll in or change a Marketplace health plan for coverage that can begin January 1.

Visit ➡️ https://t.co/jVRqJzbdzi to compare plans and get covered.

Our office here to help — call us at (603) 226-1002. Your health can’t wait — and neither should you.

If you miss tonight’s deadline, you can still sign up during Open Enrollment, but coverage won’t start until February 1 for plans selected after today.

Since day one on this job, I’ve been working to cut the sky-high costs of healthcare that are crushing hardworking Granite Staters. Our bipartisan bill to save healthcare for millions of Americans now has the support of 218 Members of Congress, but the Speaker of the House refuses to allow a vote.   

The American people deserve on our bipartisan bill. Enough grandstanding, Mr. Speaker. Let’s get this done.

.@SpeakerJohnson: hardworking Americans are days away from losing their healthcare. Our commonsense bipartisan bill will prevent a death spiral and save healthcare for people across New Hampshire. Enough with the obstruction and grandstanding. Time to bring our bill up for a vote.

Today, America’s servicemembers, veterans, and military families are forced to fight endless red tape and navigate a confusing and deeply frustrating system to get the healthcare they have earned.

That’s not right. 

That’s why I am leading on a commonsense, bipartisan bill called the Military CARE Act, which will cut senseless red tape, restore basic accountability, and return the power back where it belongs: with patients.

Fear is contagious, but courage is too. We saw important flickers of courage in Congress last week when 218 of us in the House joined together to force a vote on lowering your healthcare costs. Our work is far from over, and I will continue working with anyone who will work with me to lower your healthcare costs. 

🎥 @amaricas_const

A bipartisan group of 218 of us in the House came together to force a vote on lowering your healthcare costs, but the Speaker of the House of Representatives continues to obstruct a vote on lowering costs and saving healthcare. Enough — we have got to get this done. https://t.co/VFMETWcCqg
